role: two-way Base44-GitHub synchronization, ownership, CI, database and deployment contract

source_of_truth.base44_role: synchronized customer-facing web/product builder and preview surface
source_of_truth.rule: Two-way sync may move source changes between Base44 and GitHub, but GitHub history/review plus CACE CI remain the merge/deployment authority.

preferred.description: Base44 syncs with the CACE repository but has a narrow write zone. Protected paths are guarded by policy, CI and review.

strongest_isolation.description: If Base44 cannot honor the protected monorepo workflow reliably, sync Base44 with a dedicated CACE web repository and consume versioned public API/schema contracts from Cace-app.

ownership_rules: Base44 may edit base44-owned paths directly through two-way sync.
Joint-review paths require a normal GitHub PR/review and the applicable CACE checks before merge.
Base44 must not directly edit CACE-protected paths. It should propose a typed API/schema requirement instead.
Generated/read-only paths must be regenerated from canonical source rather than hand-edited.

If a feature cannot be completed inside the Base44 write zone, Base44 must preserve the current architecture and emit the required private API/schema change rather than reimplementing protected semantics.

version_control_allowed: seed/test fixtures that contain no production data or secrets
never_sync_to_git: protein sequences/coordinates unless explicitly public fixture data
database_boundary.mirror_rule: Base44 may hold a customer-facing read model/status mirror, but proof/evidence/wallet/scientific truth stays authoritative in the private CACE service plane.

ci_hierarchy.authority: deterministic affected-check planner; never proof evidence
authoritative engineering merge gate for Python/C++/web/policy/security regression

base44_may_deploy: approved Base44-managed customer/product services that do not own CACE scientific/proof/wallet authority
deployment.production_rule: Only reviewed GitHub commits that pass required CACE gates may become production CACE releases. A Base44 preview/publish event is not by itself a CACE production-release attestation.

secrets.rule: Use deployment secret stores/connectors. Two-way GitHub sync must never be used as a secret transport.

rules: Base44 cannot edit theorem source, proof contracts, proof ledger, canonical qualification metadata, or proof-sensitive CI without protected review.
Base44 may render customer-safe proof status returned by typed CACE APIs.
Base44 may render customer-safe LaTeX proof views without receiving proprietary theorem source or hidden proof-search traces.

protected_change_protocol.base44_action: stop direct edit and create a GitHub-visible requirement/proposal describing the typed API/schema change needed
protected_change_protocol.cace_action: implement/review protected change on a normal CACE branch
protected_change_protocol.sync_back: after merge, two-way sync returns the reviewed public contract/UI-compatible change to Base44
protected_change_protocol.no_bypass: do not duplicate protected logic in Base44 to avoid the review boundary

production_acceptance: two-way sync round-trip does not modify protected paths unexpectedly
Base44-owned changes pass Base44 checks plus CACE Build Lite and relevant GitHub engineering gates
protected-path change attempted by a Base44 sync branch fails the sync-boundary guard
generated/read-only paths cannot be hand-edited by Base44 workflow
database schema changes are versioned while production rows remain outside Git
Base44 preview cannot promote proof/evidence/wallet/scientific truth
production deployment references an exact reviewed GitHub commit
rollback to a prior reviewed GitHub commit is documented and tested
repo_settings_required: Require pull requests before merging protected branches.
Require CODEOWNERS review for protected paths where supported.
Require CACE engineering checks before merge.
Do not allow Base44 integration credentials to bypass branch protection.
Configure BASE44_GITHUB_ACTOR repository variable once the actual GitHub actor/app identity is known.
Prefer Base44-originated branches/pull requests or another reviewable integration path rather than direct production-main writes.
